title: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’
slides: Why is Apple's CEO warning against AI for AI's sake?
Tim Cook says Apple asks if AI truly helps users.
That's the opposite of rivals racing to add AI features.
Expect fewer AI features, but more useful ones on your iPhone.
Ask: does this AI tool actually solve your problem?
thread_text:
1. The AI race has a new critic

Tim Cook says Apple won't add AI just to keep up with rivals. While Google and Microsoft rush features out the door, Apple is asking a harder question.

2. The question Apple asks first

Does this AI actually help the user? Cook says every feature must pass that test before it ships — a slow, deliberate filter rivals seem to skip.

3. Rivals are racing, Apple is filtering

Google and Microsoft are shipping AI tools fast to win the hype cycle. Apple's slower approach bets that users care more about usefulness than feature count.

4. What this means for your iPhone

Expect fewer AI features on iOS, but each one vetted for real-world value. The bet: less noise, more tools you'll actually open twice.

5. Test your own AI tools today

Pick one AI feature you use and ask: does it solve a real problem? If not, drop it. Apply Cook's filter to your own stack this week.
